items.summary: کاخ سفید از کیمبرلی گیلفویل خواسته است تا از سمت سفیر ایالات متحده در یونان استعفا دهد و این در حالی است که اتهامات فزاینده ای در رابطه با معاملات مالی، رفتار با کارکنان سفارت و روابط با منافع تجاری خارجی دارد. کیتی زاخاریا، سخنگوی کاخ سفید روز سه شنبه در اولین نشست خبری خود با مطبوعات اعلام کرد: "ما از سفیر گیلفویل درخواست کرده ایم که استعفا دهد. او یک سرمایه فوق العاده برای تیم بوده است و ما برای او آرزوی موفقیت داریم." مشخص نیست که آیا گیلفویل استعفای رسمی خود را ارائه کرده است یا خیر، و هنگامی که از او برای شفافیت خواسته شد، کاخ سفید فاکس نیوز دیجیتال را به اظهارات در جلسه توجیهی ارجاع داد. این به روز رسانی از زکریا تنها یک روز پس از آن منتشر شد که دونالد ترامپ، رئیس جمهور آمریکا علناً اذعان کرد که در حال بررسی اخراج گیلفویل است که قبلا با پسر بزرگش، دونال نامزد کرده بود.
items.summary_original: The White House has asked Kimberly Guilfoyle to resign as U.S. ambassador to Greece amid mounting allegations involving her financial dealings, treatment of embassy staff and relationships with foreign business interests. "We have asked Ambassador Guilfoyle to resign. She has been a wonderful asset to the team, and we wish her well," White House press secretary Katie Zacharia announced Tuesday during her first-ever briefing to the press. It is not clear whether Guilfoyle lodged her official resignation, and when asked for clarity, the White House referred Fox News Digital to the remarks from the briefing. The update from Zacharia came just one day after President Donald Trump publicly acknowledged that he was considering firing Guilfoyle, who was previously engaged to his eldest son, Donald Trump Jr. TRUMP 'LOOKING AT' FIRING AMBASSADOR TO GREECE: 'WE'RE NOT HAPPY' "Well, we're looking at it," Trump told reporters Monday when asked whether he was considering removing Guilfoyle. "We're not happy." Guilfoyle came under scrutiny last week after The Wall Street Journal reported that she asked Trump donor Eric Deters to pay off a $100,000 American Express bill shortly before her Senate confirmation hearing in July 2025. items.summary_original: Pope Leo XIV arrived at Agostino Gemelli University Hospital in Rome for a procedure to remove a small node on his lung on Tuesday. The 71-year-old pontiff said Monday that doctors discovered the nodule at a "very early stage" and recommended its removal. The surgery is not expected to last long, and the pope is expected to remain hospitalized for approximately one week, according to Vatican spokesman Matteo Bruni . "Doctors found a small lump in the lung," Leo said after an Angelus address at St. Peter's Square on Monday. "It was identified at a very early stage and well situated." POPE LEO ANNOUNCES TUMOR ON LUNG, SURGERY PLANNED IN 'NEXT FEW DAYS' "The doctors consider it appropriate to intervene and so, following their advice, I decided to have surgery to remove it," he continued. "The surgery is already scheduled for the next few days. I thank you for your spiritual closeness and I rely on your prayer." The surgery is likely to take place within a few days at the Gemelli Hospital in Rome, which is known as the "Pope's" hospital, Vatican sources told Fox News. POPE LEO XIV BEGINS HISTORIC 4-DAY VISIT TO FRANCE The Vatican has not disclosed whether the nodule is cancerous, and no further details about the pope's diagnosis or the planned procedure were immediately available. items.summary_original: There are two big differences between the previous Trump-era midterms and this year’s contest. The first is the president’s approval rating, which is lower now than it was during President Donald Trump’s first term in 2018 or President Joe Biden’s term in 2022. The second is Democrats’ generic ballot lead, which is wider and more enduring than it was in the 2018 "blue wave" election and much larger than the edge the GOP had in 2022. Combined with Democrats’ candidate quality improvements and a Republican-led redistricting effort that could fall short of expectations, the House is likely out of reach for the GOP this year. REPUBLICANS FACE BRUTAL MIDTERM HEADWINDS. SIX FORCES COULD HELP THEM DEFY HISTORY. Then there’s a similarity: in all three elections, the Senate has been in play right up until the finish line. In Trump’s first term, the Republicans ended up gaining two Senate seats despite a gloomy national environment. Four years ago, with inflation surging, the Democrats managed to add a Senate seat to their tally. 12 RACES SCRAMBLE SENATE BATTLEFIELD AS DEMOCRATS EYE COMEBACK The Democrats have plentiful paths to 51 seats on election night. Republicans keep plowing money into six toss-up states, plus Kansas, and those efforts haven’t much moved the needle. Yet the GOP’s paths to 50 are getting wider. items.summary_original: A Senate Republican running for re-election in ruby-red South Dakota has joined a growing number of candidates putting distance between themselves and President Donald Trump . But it’s more subtle than Republicans opposing the Iran war or dodging Trump campaign visits as Election Day nears and his popularity struggles. Just last month, Trump’s name and endorsement were featured prominently on Republican South Dakota Sen. Mike Rounds’ campaign website, but some mentions of the president have since been scrubbed, according to an older version of the website reviewed by Fox News Digital. SLEEPER SENATE RACE EMERGES AS UNEXPECTED HEADACHE FOR REPUBLICANS AHEAD OF MIDTERMS Rounds’ campaign noted to Fox News Digital that not every mention of Trump has been removed. "The president’s endorsement is still front and center on the website in Mike’s announcement video," Rounds’ campaign advisor, Rob Skjonsberg, told Fox News Digital. "But, generally speaking, it’s not abnormal to hone in on general election messaging." Trump endorsed Rounds last year and lauded the lawmaker as an "incredibly strong advocate for the wonderful people of South Dakota, a State I love, and WON BIG, in 2016, 2020, and 2024!" "Mike Rounds has my Complete and Total Endorsement for Re-Election — HE WILL NEVER LET YOU DOWN," Trump said on Truth Social at the time. items.summary_original: President Donald Trump is "looking at" firing U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle after mounting reports alleging improper conduct before and during her tenure in Athens. "Well, we’re looking at it," Trump told reporters at the White House before leaving for an Ohio campaign rally Monday afternoon. "Yeah, we’re not happy." Trump’s comments came after a senior U.S. official said Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio were "extremely pissed off" by reports about Guilfoyle’s conduct and expected to make a decision on her future this week. TRUMP AND RUBIO WEIGH FIRING KIMBERLY GUILFOYLE AS MISCONDUCT AND DONOR BAILOUT ALLEGATIONS MOUNT The Wall Street Journal has reported a series of allegations involving Guilfoyle, including that she asked a Trump donor to pay a $100,000 credit card bill before her confirmation hearing while allegedly promising access to administration officials. The Journal also reported claims that Guilfoyle made a threat involving the Greek government, promoted the interests of a Greek construction and energy company, allowed a lobbyist into private diplomatic meetings and accepted improper gifts or services. Rubio, who was in Greece last week, was frustrated by reporters repeatedly asking him to address the allegations publicly. items.summary: ارتش ایالات متحده از طرح خود برای آماده سازی سربازان برای مبارزه از طریق حملات بیولوژیکی به جای اینکه تصور کند هر تهدیدی را می توان متوقف کرد، رونمایی کرد. طرحی که به تازگی امضا شده است که سناریوهای جنگ بیولوژیکی را به آموزش های رزمی معمولی وارد می کند زیرا هوش مصنوعی (AI) و بیوتکنولوژی نگرانی های جدیدی را در مورد سلاح هایی که دشمنان آمریکا می توانند در آینده نزدیک توسعه دهند، ایجاد می کند. دکتر آلیسون تاماسی، یک مقام ارشد در آژانس هسته‌ای و مقابله با سلاح‌های کشتار جمعی ارتش، روز دوشنبه به خبرنگاران گفت: "آیا می‌توانیم از هر سرباز در برابر هر تهدید زیستی احتمالی محافظت کنیم؟ احتمالاً نه." او افزود: "ما نمی توانیم آنها را در یک حباب قرار دهیم." این تغییر در حالی صورت می گیرد که مقامات آمریکایی به ارزیابی ادامه می دهند که آیا مسکو برنامه تسلیحات بیولوژیکی تهاجمی خود را پس از مرگ مرموز در روسیه که با یک حمله ضد جنگ مرتبط بود حفظ می کند یا خیر.
items.summary_original: The U.S. Army unveiled its plan to prepare soldiers to fight through biological attacks rather than assume every threat can be stopped. The newly signed plan bringing biological warfare scenarios into routine combat training as artificial intelligence (AI) and biotechnology raise new concerns about the weapons America's adversaries could develop in the near future. "Can we protect every soldier from every possible bio threat? Probably not," Dr. Alison Tamasi, a senior official at the Army's Nuclear and Countering Weapons of Mass Destruction Agency, told reporters on Monday. "We can't put them in a bubble," she added. The shift comes as U.S. officials continue to assess whether Moscow maintains an offensive biological weapons program after a mysterious death in Russia was linked to an anti-plague facility — reviving questions of biological safety and transparency. CHINESE AI MODEL INVESTIGATED AFTER RESEARCHER SAYS IT PROVIDED INSTRUCTIONS FOR BIOWEAPONS, ASSASSINATIONS Still, the Army hopes their implemented plan will help prepare the force to deploy and fight in biologically contested environments by 2035. Rather than treating outbreaks primarily as medical emergencies, the military wants commanders, intelligence officers and logistics personnel to prepare for biological threats while continuing to carry out their combat missions. items.summary_original: Rep. María Elvira Salazar , R-Fla., is touting an endorsement from Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella as she seeks re-election to Congress. In a video that the lawmaker posted, the foreign leader, speaking in Spanish, referred to Salazar as his nation's "best friend" in America's Congress. The foreign leader is a Colombian American citizen who owns property located in the U.S. lawmaker's congressional district, and he and his wife have previously given nearly $90,000 to Salazar, NBC News reported. 'GONE TOO FAR:' GOP CANDIDATE RUNS TO TRUMP'S LEFT ON SIGNATURE ISSUE IN DEEP RED DISTRICT "And I receive with immense pride the support of my friend, President Abelardo de la Espriella," Salazar wrote in part of a Spanish-language post on X, which included the video of the foreign official supporting her. "Representing thousands of Colombians in South Florida has made Colombia a cause I carry with me every day to Congress," she noted in the post. "Abelardo has in me a friend. Colombia, an ally. And Colombians, a steadfast voice in the United States Congress." HOUSE GOP LAWMAKER UNDER FIRE BY FELLOW REPUBLICANS AFTER AD BASHING TRUMP ON IMMIGRATION Salazar backed de la Espriella for election earlier this year. The lawmaker, who is currently running for re-election, is facing Democratic challenger Eliott Rodriguez. REPUBLICAN REP MARIA ELVIRA SALAZAR DECLARES, 'AFTER CUBA, NICARAGUA IS NEXT' Salazar has served in the House since early 2021.

items.summary_original: The White House is set to end a weekslong stretch without a permanent press secretary at the podium Tuesday when Katie Zacharia makes her briefing room debut, succeeding Karoline Leavitt after a shake-up in President Donald Trump's communications team. "I am pleased to announce that Katie Zacharia will be beginning her term as Press Secretary tomorrow, Columbus Day, and will be doing an introductory News Conference on Tuesday at 9:30 A.M. from the Press Briefing Room in the White House. Katie has been with me, in spirit, from the very beginning, and will do a fantastic job!" Trump said on Truth Social Sunday. Zacharia, an attorney and television commentator, served as senior communications adviser to Trump Media Technology Group, which operates the president's social media platform, Truth Social. Her appointment follows Leavitt's departure from the White House in August. During his first administration, President Donald Trump had four White House press secretaries: Sean Spicer, Sarah Huckabee Sanders , Stephanie Grisham and Kayleigh McEnany. New Jersey is a blue state that has trended redder in recent years, with President Donald Trump flipping key areas in 2024. However, 1972 was the last time a Republican won a U.S. Senate election in the state, when Sen. Clifford Case was re-elected. Sens. Nick Brady in 1982 and Jeff Chiesa in 2013 later served brief, appointed terms. Murphy, an attorney from the Pine Barrens, earned loud applause for his response to a question about Iran when asked what he would tell Trump if the president called him for advice on the conflict. items.summary_original: DAVENPORT, Iowa — As Iowa emerges as one of the most critical states in the midterm election in both House and Senate races, Fox News Digital spoke with local Republican candidates about what the media is getting right and wrong on the ground in the Hawkeye State. As local conservatives gathered at a Scott County Republican Party event near downtown Davenport in early October to watch the first gubernatorial debate, a month out from the consequential midterm election, Fox News Digital was there asking if the media narrative was accurate that Iowa was primed for a "blue wave" amid concerns about President Donald Trump’s economy, gas prices, and the war in Iran . Greg Guy, running as a Republican for treasurer in Scott County, acknowledged that Iowans are "concerned" about the price of gas, but believes they understand that the surge in cost is likely temporary after the war in Iran winds down. items.summary_original: A heckler wearing a "Release the Epstein Files" shirt was punched in the face by an apparent supporter of President Donald Trump during a rally Monday in Youngstown, Ohio, before the president mocked the protester's weight. Trump was criticizing Ohio Democratic Senate candidate Sherrod Brown, who is challenging Republican Sen. Jon Husted after losing his Senate seat in 2024, when rally attendees shifted their attention toward a confrontation in the crowd. Video of the confrontation showed a rallygoer who appeared to support Trump shoving the heckler and striking her in the face as the crowd chanted "USA!" TRUMP TOUTS ‘GOLDEN AGE’ AT OHIO RALLY, URGES VOTERS TO DELIVER GOP MIDTERM WINS The man also grabbed the woman by the hair and attempted to slam her face toward the ground. Police eventually intervened and broke up the fight before escorting the woman out of the venue. Video showed the man who struck her remaining in the arena and exchanging high-fives with other attendees. Trump appeared to notice the disruption and accused the protester of being paid to interrupt the rally, although he offered no evidence to support the allegation. He also mocked the protester's weight. "Should the adversary choose to press the attack or commit his reserves, we will break the warfighting system engaged against us," U.S. Air Force Gen. Alexus Grynkewich said at the Warsaw Security Forum in Poland , in an apparent warning to Moscow. "This includes not just the attacking force itself, but anything and everything that supports, sustains, and controls that force," he said during a panel titled "Theory of Victory: How Do We Achieve Military Success Against Russia in Deterrence and Defence?" on the first day of the forum. "If someone is foolish enough to attack us, we will fight," he said. "We will stop the attack and deny them the ability to achieve their objectives, whatever those might be. Martin was pressed during an interview on MSNOW about whether the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) is a liability for the party ahead of the midterm elections . "So let me just say, I've always taken a big-tent approach to how you build a party," Martin said. "That's why I was successful for all these years in Minnesota. I believe you win through addition, not subtraction. You win by growing your coalition, not shrinking it." NEWSOM TELLS DEMOCRATS TO BE IN THE 'ADDITION NOT SUBTRACTION' BUSINESS WITH SOCIALISTS "And sometimes, is there a middle ground, though, when Americans see that…" interjected MSNOW anchor Peter Alexander. "No, not at all, because that's where the vast majority of Americans are at," Martin replied. "Maybe right in the middle, or a little center-left, or a little center-right. But it doesn't mean we can't bring new voices into the party, right? Of course, we have to keep growing and we have to keep expanding this tent," Martin reiterated. "When the government uses force against a New Yorker, the standard for accountability must be at its highest," Mamdani said in a press release. "Every New Yorker deserves to know that force will be used lawfully, carefully and only when necessary." More than nine months after taking office, Mamdani has yet to fulfill several campaign pledges, including disbanding the NYPD's Strategic Response Group, eliminating its database of suspected gang members and shifting police resources away from low-level offenses. items.summary_original: Gun owners will no longer be required to federally register or seek advance approval to manufacture or transfer silencers, short-barreled rifles, short-barreled shotguns and "Any Other Weapons" (AOWs), the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) announced Friday. The policy directive halts National Firearms Act (NFA) enforcement for items subject to zero-dollar tax rates under the updated guidelines. In a letter to federal firearms licensees, ATF Director Robert Cekada noted that the move follows a federal court decision invalidating key manufacturing and transfer provisions of the NFA. GUN RIGHTS GETS 'GREATEST RESTORATION' IN 100 YEARS WITH LATEST TRUMP DOJ MOVE, LAWMAKER HAILS "The direction from the President, Congress, and the courts is clear," Cekada said. "ATF is now following suit with our enforcement posture while continuing to ensure we remain focused where we are needed the most: combatting violent crime in American communities." The regulatory shift stems from the One Big Beautiful Bill Act , in which Congress reduced NFA manufacturing and transfer taxes to $0 for silencers, short-barreled rifles, short-barreled shotguns, and AOWs. "چرا مردم می خواهند آن را ببینند؟" جولیا ویلسون، کارمند غیرنظامی سابق وزارت دفاع که 17 سال پیش از تیراندازی جان سالم به در برد، به فاکس نیوز دیجیتال گفت. ویلسون می خواهد تیرانداز دسته جمعی اعدام شود، و به عنوان یک قربانی، می خواهد در اعدام او شرکت کند و به چشمان او نگاه کند. حسن، یک روانپزشک ارتش در آن زمان، در 5 نوامبر 2009 وارد مرکز آمادگی سربازی در تگزاس A شد.
items.summary_original: A survivor of the 2009 Fort Hood massacre says she wishes the mass shooter could be killed one time for every life he took that day – but even she is questioning the military's decision to livestream his death. Nidal Hasan, 56, is scheduled to face execution by firing squad on Dec. 3, 2026, and Secretary of War Pete Hegset h announced earlier this month that it will be made available to stream to the public. "Why would people want to see that?" Julia Wilson, a former Defense Department civilian employee who survived the shooting 17 years ago, told Fox News Digital. Wilson wants the mass shooter executed, and, as a victim, she wants to attend his execution and look him in the eye. Hasan, an Army psychiatrist at the time, walked into a soldier readiness center on Nov. 5, 2009, on the Texas Army post and opened fire, killing 13 people and wounding 32 others. Following a military court-martial verdict, Hasan was sentenced to death on Aug. 28, 2013. FORT HOOD SURVIVOR SHOT IN HEAD VOWS TO WATCH TERRORIST FACE HISTORIC FIRING SQUAD On Oct. 2, President Donald Trump approved the death sentence, and days later Hegseth announced it would be by a public firing squad. "Personally, I do want to be there," Wilson told Fox News Digital. "I do want to look him in the eye to let him know, ‘Look, I may have been your victim that day, but I'm not your victim anymore. I survived you. My child survived you, a lot of us survived you. You didn't do as much damage as you thought you were going to.'

items.summary_original: Adventurer Karl Bushby has finally stepped foot on UK soil after a 28-year journey across the world. On Oct. 5, he announced he swam the English Channel , from France to England. While resting in Dover, he said, "I’m staring at the Union Jack flying outside this hotel. I’ve seen many flags over the days, but that one is special." On social media he shared one of his first meals back, overjoyed to have authentic British fish and chips again. DALE 'GREY BEARD' SANDERS RECLAIMS TITLE AS OLDEST PERSON TO THRU-HIKE THE APPALACHIAN TRAIL AT 91 His journey is not over yet. He hopes to reach the finish line — his mother’s home in Hull — by the end of the month. According to his website , he received a birthday card in the 1990s from his father about two soldiers arguing over an impossible feat, walking from London to New York via the Bering Strait. Karl grabbed a map and drew a single line, knowing he found his life’s mission. items.summary_original: A Biden-appointed federal judge who previously drew a formal misconduct complaint from President Donald Trump's Justice Department for alleged bias erupted at government lawyers again Monday, in a heated showdown over rapid tree removal at a historic golf course on national parkland. Judge Ana Reyes unleashed her latest rebuke during an emergency hearing over hundreds of trees removed from East Potomac Golf Links in Hains Point, D.C. Trump wants to transform the historic public facility into a championship-caliber golf course like his courses in the U.S., Ireland and Scotland – the latest courtroom collision between the administration and its political opponents. Journalist Scott MacFarlane, who live-tweeted from the hearing, described Reyes as "scream[ing]" at administration attorneys over the government's late-Friday notification that tree removal would begin Saturday. A government lawyer acknowledged that approximately 430 trees had already been cut down, according to MacFarlane. OBAMA-APPOINTED JUDGE TORCHES TRUMP ADMIN IN LATEST COURTROOM SHOWDOWN, REFERS ATTORNEY FOR BAR REVIEW "You've lost credibility!" Reyes told government attorneys, according to MacFarlane's live courtroom reporting. The administration maintains that the removals implement a 2019 National Park Service landscape-restoration plan predating Trump's redesign proposal for the links, which sit on an island connected to the city proper by the Jefferson Memorial and Francis Case Bridge at its western edge.

items.summary_original: With just over three weeks to go until Election Day , more and more red states and congressional districts appear in reach for the Democrats, as they work to win back House and Senate majorities from the Republicans in the midterms. But a massive Republican spending advantage threatens to complicate those ambitions. Republican campaigns, committees and aligned groups have outspent their Democratic counterparts by $400 million so far this election cycle, according to AdImpact, a leading political advertising tracking firm. The disparity is forcing Democrats to make difficult decisions about where to invest and how much to spend as the party tries to expand the electoral map . "We are being outspent by the Republicans. That's just a fact," Lauren French, communications director at the Senate Majority PAC, told Fox News Digital. "In many of these states, they have really transactionalized elections, so they have monopoly money to play with, whereas we are working with real resources." DEMOCRATS THINK A BLUE WAVE IS FORMER - HERE ARE THREE FACTORS THAT COULD STOP IT The latest Fox News Power Rankings shifted GOP-dominated South Carolina from Solid to Likely Republican. The Senate showdown in reliably Republican Kansas is Lean Republican, while the races in red-leaning Alaska, Iowa, Ohio and Texas are rated toss-ups. items.summary_original: In one of the most hotly contested governor's races in the country, the Democratic nominee has been working overtime to cultivate a moderate image — while reportedly attending a church that openly embraces some of the progressive causes dividing voters in Iowa. Rob Sand, Iowa’s state auditor and its Democratic nominee for governor, regularly attended Plymouth Congregational United Church of Christ, located in the state’s capital, as of late 2025, according to a local journalist. Over the years, Plymouth has hosted and promoted drag queen performances, invited a transgender pastor to serve as a guest pastor and openly supported abortion. Sand has emphasized his faith on the campaign trail, repeatedly referencing Christianity and quoting scripture, at times successfully appealing to otherwise conservative Iowans. In addition to leaning on his faith, Sand has repeatedly described himself as independently minded, claimed to have voted for Republicans in the past and said that he sometimes prefers working with the GOP over Democrats, calling political parties "poison." "I am a Christian. I’m a conservative. But I’m not a party-based person," one voter is quoted as saying in a Sand press release. "I like to vote for the person as opposed to the party. And to me, (Sand) just seems really honest and down to earth. And I enjoyed him." "There's been countless CEOs and major heads of companies that have moved their businesses to Palm Beach," she said, pointing to Florida's favorable tax climate and lifestyle as major draws. The two are running again on a joint slate in the upcoming elections. "مجازات اعدام غیرقابل پذیرش است زیرا حمله به مصونیت و حیثیت افراد است. منفعت عمومی را می توان حفظ کرد و الزامات عدالت را می توان بدون توسل به مجازات اعدام برآورده کرد: سیستم های موثر بازداشت توسعه یافته اند که از شهروندان محافظت می کند و در عین حال مجرمان را کاملاً محروم نمی کند.
items.summary_original: Pope Leo XIV condemned the death penalty as "inadmissible" as the Pentagon faces criticism over plans to livestream an execution later this year. Leo, the first American pope, shared his opposition to capital punishment Saturday in a social media post marking World Day Against the Death Penalty. Citing Catholic doctrine revised under his predecessor, Pope Francis, Leo emphasized that the death penalty violates human dignity. "The death penalty is inadmissible because it is an attack on the inviolability and dignity of the person. The common good can be safeguarded and the requirements of justice can be met without recourse to capital punishment: effective systems of detention have been developed that protect citizens while at the same time do not completely deprive those who are guilty of the possibility of redemption," Leo wrote on X. "#NoDeathPenalty," he added in the post. VETERAN SHOT 7 TIMES IN FORT HOOD MASSACRE HAS A WARNING FOR AMERICANS PLANNING TO WATCH EXECUTION In 2018, Francis revised the Catholic Church's official position on capital punishment, declaring the death penalty "inadmissible" in all circumstances. "Consequently the church teaches, in the light of the Gospel, that the death penalty is inadmissible because it is an attack on the inviolability and dignity of the person," the revised Catechism states. items.summary_original: At least 139 migrants, including 15 children, died when a boat carrying more than 300 people capsized off the coast of Djibouti, according to the United Nations' migration agency. The vessel was carrying 305 people from Djibouti toward Yemen when it capsized Thursday night or early Friday near Guhere, north of Obock, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) said Sunday. At least 84 people remained missing as of Sunday, while more than 80 survived. All the survivors were Ethiopian nationals , according to the agency. "No one gets into a boat like that unless they believe there is no other safe way," IOM Director General Amy Pope said in a statement. I am asking governments and donors to act before the next boat goes down," Pope added. The confirmed death toll includes only victims buried by authorities in Djibouti and could rise as additional bodies are verified, IOM Chief of Mission in Djibouti Alexandre Coissac told The Associated Press. items.summary_original: Iran-backed Houthis launched a series of attacks on Saudi Arabian airports through Sunday, reportedly killing at least 14 people, including an American, and injuring more than 300 others, according to reports . The attacks heightened fears of a wider Middle East war as regional experts warned of "cross-domain escalation" amid heightened tensions over Washington's September actions against Iran's aviation sector. The Houthis claimed responsibility for earlier attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, while U.S. officials blamed the Iran-backed group for Saturday's strike, which reportedly killed 13 people and injured more than 300. SAUDI FOREIGN MINISTER WARNS HOUTHI THREAT GOES GLOBAL AS TRUMP HOLDS FIRE Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority said another attack on Sunday killed a Pakistani resident and injured 11 others. Meanwhile, an airport in Dammam, in the kingdom's Eastern Province, was also reportedly targeted by the Houthis. "Cross-domain escalation by Iran and its proxies will continue to be a primary strategy," Behnam Ben Taleblu , senior director of the Iran Program and a senior fellow at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, told Fox News Digital on Sunday. "The emphasis on aviation targets connects directly to the closing of Iran's aviation sector and sanctions imposed on its commercial airlines under the U.S. maximum pressure campaign," he warned. items.summary_original: Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei claimed Oct. 8 that U.S. and Israeli strikes had failed to undermine Iran's domestic security forces, praising police personnel for resisting attacks launched in February under Operations Epic Fury and Roaring Lion. Khamenei's remarks on X also came as the U.S. Army released a new battlefield identification guide to help American troops recognize members of Iran's conventional military, known as the Artesh, whose ground forces were estimated by the Jerusalem Institute for Strategy and Security in June at 350,000 personnel. "The criminal US-Zionist enemy's desperate efforts and malicious attacks on the pillars of social order and security, which are unparalleled throughout history, have not caused the courageous personnel of the Police Force to waver even a fraction in their mission," Khamenei wrote in a statement. Khamenei specifically praised Iran's Law Enforcement Command, known as FARAJA, accusing the United States and Israel of targeting the institution responsible for maintaining domestic order. "The focus and persistence of the criminal US-Zionist enemy in striking at the Police Force at its various levels, from its highest command levels down to those who are on the frontline, has only served to underscore the paramount importance of this institution more than ever," he wrote. items.summary_original: More than two decades after being elected to what was supposed to be a four-year term, Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas has once again postponed elections, extending a nearly 20-year wait for voters to choose a new legislature. Abbas issued a decree Friday pushing Palestinian Legislative Council elections from next month to Sept. 11, 2027, according to the official Palestinian news agency WAFA. Presidential elections , which have not been held since Abbas' 2005 victory, are also scheduled for that date. The delay allows Palestinian leaders to remain in power without facing voters and could further damage the credibility of the Palestinian Authority, which has faced criticism over corruption and its security cooperation with Israel. NICARAGUA'S ORTEGA SAYS COUNTRY WILL 'NEVER AGAIN' HOLD ELECTIONS, SHUTTING OUT OPPOSITION The Palestinian Authority, dominated by Abbas' Fatah party, governs parts of the West Bank under agreements reached in the 1990s. Palestinian officials cited conditions in the West Bank, Gaza Strip and east Jerusalem as reasons for postponing the vote. The Palestine Liberation Organization's Executive Committee, which Abbas heads, claimed Israel had blocked election materials and international observers from entering Gaza, according to The Associated Press. items.summary_original: Pope Leo XIV announced Sunday that he will undergo surgery to remove a small nodule from his lung, revealing the unexpected health concern to thousands of faithful gathered in St. Peter's Square following his traditional Angelus prayer. The 71-year-old pontiff said doctors discovered the nodule at a "very early stage" and recommended its removal. The surgery is scheduled for the coming days, with the pope expected to remain hospitalized for approximately one week, according to Vatican spokesman Matteo Bruni . And had an ominous warning, "What you’re seeing in London and other European cities can easily happen in the U.S… These cultural shifts will all come to America, unless American leaders are willing to fight back." items.summary_original: As Israel prepared to assassinate Hezbollah leader Hassan Nasrallah in September 2024, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his senior defense officials disagreed over whether to notify the Biden administration ahead of the operation, fearing Washington could try to stop the mission, according to Wall Street Journal editorial writer Elliot Kaufman and a second source familiar with the deliberations. "140%, they won't approve of the mission," Netanyahu told senior Israeli defense officials, according to Kaufman, co-author of " In the War Room: The Inside Story of Israel's Fight Against Hamas and the Iranian Axis ," who recounted the exchange in an interview with Fox News Digital. Then-Defense Minister Yoav Gallant and IDF Chief of Staff Herzi Halevi favored informing Washington, believing the Americans might support a strike against a Hezbollah leader linked to the deaths of U.S. service members, according to Kaufman. Netanyahu, however, warned that then-U.S. National Security Adviser Jake Sullivan would "jump out of his skin" if he learned of the plans. The disagreement reflected a widening divide between Jerusalem and Washington over Israel's military campaign against Iran's regional proxies, as the Biden administration sought to prevent the fighting from escalating into a broader regional war. items.summary_original: JERUSALEM — A growing number of Israeli army battlefield life-saving measures have emerged during the Iranian regime-backed multi-front war against the Jewish state, and those new technologies are helping the U.S. too. Fox News Digital was briefed on the most current insights and data on Israel’s success rate in saving soldiers’ lives from a senior Israel Defense Forces (IDF) medical specialist in battlefield medicine. The grueling Israeli ground offensive against the U.S.-designated terrorist movement Hamas in the Gaza Strip, which started in October 2023, after the organization’s invasion of Israel on Oct. 7, introduced cutting-edge medical tactics to the battlefield. THE US-ISRAEL STRATEGIC ALLIANCE – PARTNERSHIP, NOT CHARITY Hamas brutally murdered over 1,200 people in southern Israel, including more than 40 Americans, and kidnapped 251 people. items.summary_original: A powerful 7.7 magnitude earthquake struck off Panama's southern coast Friday, shaking the country's capital as officials investigated a potential tsunami threat. The U.S. Geological Survey initially measured the earthquake at magnitude 8.0 before lowering its estimate to 7.7. The quake struck at 1:56 p.m. ET, at a depth of 7.8 miles, near Pitaloza Arriba, Panama. A 5.5 magnitude aftershock followed, with its epicenter approximately 50 miles east of the initial earthquake. The Panama Canal said operations were continuing normally following Friday's earthquake, with emergency protocols activated and technical teams inspecting facilities for possible damage. Canal officials said their priority was ensuring the safety of workers, vessels, crews and nearby communities as assessments continued. MORE THAN 3,000 MISSING AFTER COLOMBIA EARTHQUAKE AS TRUMP ADMINISTRATION PROVIDES $15.5 MILLION IN RELIEF The earthquake was felt in Panama City and in San José, the capital of neighboring Costa Rica , according to Reuters. Tsunami officials warned that waves reaching 3 to 10 feet above tide levels were possible along some coastal areas of Panama, while parts of Ecuador could experience waves of approximately 1 to 3 feet. Smaller tsunami waves of less than 1 foot above tide levels were forecast for coastal areas of Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, El Salvador, Guatemala, Mexico, Nicaragua and Peru. items.summary: نوانتم «ناوی» پیلای، حقوقدان باتجربه ای که ریاست کمیسیون سازمان ملل متحد را بر عهده داشت که به این نتیجه رسید که اسرائیل در غزه نسل کشی کرده است، روز جمعه به دلیل «تلاش هایش برای ترویج صلح و قوانین بین المللی» برنده جایزه صلح نوبل شد. در اعطای جایزه صلح امسال، کمیته نوبل استدلال کرد که نهادهای قوی قضایی بین المللی باید بتوانند حاکمیت قانون را اجرا کنند تا امیدی به میانجیگری در تعداد فزاینده جنگ ها و درگیری ها در سراسر جهان داشته باشند. این کمیته همچنین خاطرنشان کرد که حملات سیاسی علیه قضات و خود حقوق بین الملل در حال تبدیل شدن به امری عادی است. پیلای سابقه ای طولانی و طولانی - هم به عنوان وکیل و هم به عنوان قاضی - داشته است و اخیراً به طور قطعی درگیری بین اسرائیل و حماس را بررسی کرده است. اسراییل سازمان ملل را متهم می کند که آن را در رابطه با همان رابطه جنسی قرار داده است
items.summary_original: Navanethem "Navi" Pillay, an experienced jurist who chaired a United Nations commission that concluded Israel committed genocide in Gaza, won the Nobel Peace Prize on Friday for "her efforts to promote peace and international law." In awarding this year's Peace Prize, the Nobel Committee argued strong international judicial institutions must be able to enforce the rule of law to have any hope of mediating the growing number of wars and conflicts worldwide. The committee also noted that political attacks against judges and international law itself are becoming more commonplace. Pillay has had a long, storied career — both as a lawyer and as a judge — and more recently, she has definitively weighed in on the conflict between Israel and Hamas . ISRAEL ACCUSES UN OF PLACING IT ON SAME SEXUAL VIOLENCE BLACKLIST AS HAMAS TERRORISTS, SEVERS TIES She chaired the UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory, which was created in 2021 after a flare-up in tensions between Israelis and Palestinians. In September 2025, nearly two years after the Oct. 7 attacks , the commission concluded that Israel had committed genocide against Palestinians in Gaza, while also specifically accusing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and then-Defense Minister Yoav Gallant of inciting genocide. items.summary: هنگامی که بزرگسالان جوان روز پنجشنبه به باستیل فرانسه هجوم بردند، یک رسانه کمتر شناخته شده به نام BreakThrough News به دنبال کنندگانش یک هشدار "شکستن" ارسال کرد: "دانشجویان فرانسوی در میدان باستیل در پاریس سیل کردند." اما این داستان کامل نیست. تحقیقات دیجیتال فاکس نیوز نشان داده است که یک شبکه فراملی از سازمان‌های چپ افراطی کمونیستی و سوسیالیست با استفاده از تاکتیک‌هایی که در دهه گذشته در ایالات متحده برای تشدید ناآرامی‌ها، تعمیق اختلافات و ارائه تصویری از هرج و مرج به کار گرفته شده، اعتراضات دانشجویی آتشین فرانسه را برای پیشبرد یک دستور کار سیاسی و ایدئولوژیک گسترده‌تر به کار گرفته است. در اوایل هفته، BreakThrough News تیتر دیگری را در جلوی وب سایت خود منتشر کرد: "دانش آموزان فرانسوی در اعتصاب تاریخی علیه ریاضت اقتصادی مدارس را تعطیل کردند" و "با حمایت اتحادیه ها و پیشرفت" بسیج شدند.
items.summary_original: When young adults stormed France's Bastille on Thursday, a little-known media outlet called BreakThrough News sent followers a "BREAKING" alert: "French students flood Bastille Square in Paris." But that isn't the full story. A Fox News Digital investigation has found that a transnational network of far-left communist and socialist organizations is seizing on France’s fiery student protests to advance a wider political and ideological agenda, using tactics deployed in the United States over the past decade to amplify unrest, deepen divisions and project an image of chaos. Earlier in the week, BreakThrough News splashed another headline across the front of its website: "French students shut down schools in historic strike against austerity," mobilizing "with support from unions and progressive forces." But those "progressive forces" aren't limited to students demanding education reform as part of their "Lycéenne Mobilisation," or high school student mobilization. From France to the United States, the United Kingdom, Brazil, Greece and India, adults with deep pockets are tapping France's school protests and turning a domestic education dispute into a platform for broader political and ideological confrontation. items.title_original: 2 foreign nationals breach UK base housing key US, NATO intel hub amid $556M expansion
items.summary: به گزارش خبرگزاری رویترز، دو شهروند لتونیایی که به طور قانونی در بریتانیا زندگی می کنند، بر اساس بند 4 قانون امنیت ملی بریتانیا در سال 2023، روز پنجشنبه پس از ادعای نقض حصار محیطی در RAF Molesworth، یک پایگاه نظامی حساس بریتانیا که در آن عملیات اطلاعاتی مهم ایالات متحده و ناتو قرار دارد، دستگیر شدند. این دستگیری ها تحقیقات ضدتروریسم بزرگی را در مورد نقض امنیتی در تاسیسات استراتژیک، که به عنوان یک مرکز اطلاعاتی مرکزی از فرماندهان نظامی آمریکا در سراسر اروپا و آفریقا پشتیبانی می کند، آغاز کرد. بر اساس گزارش ها، این پایگاه همچنین تحت یک توسعه 556.5 میلیون دلاری بر روی مجتمع تحلیل اطلاعات مشترک (JIAC) قرار دارد، مکانی که برای ادغام 20 تاسیسات اطلاعاتی و گنجایش بیش از 1000 پرسنل طراحی شده است. ایران تحت نظارت
items.summary_original: Two Latvian nationals legally living in the United Kingdom were arrested under Section 4 of Britain's National Security Act of 2023 Thursday after allegedly breaching a perimeter fence at RAF Molesworth, a sensitive British military base housing critical U.S. and NATO intelligence operations, Reuters reported. The arrests triggered a major counterterrorism investigation into the security breach at the strategic installation, which serves as a central intelligence hub supporting American military commanders across Europe and Africa. The base is also undergoing a $556.5 million expansion centered on the Joint Intelligence Analysis Complex (JIAC), a location designed to consolidate 20 intelligence facilities and accommodate more than 1,000 personnel, according to reports . IRAN UNDER SCRUTINY AFTER PLOT FOILED NEAR UK BASE USED BY US MILITARY The suspects, ages 32 and 36, were discovered inside the base around 2 a.m. Thursday after an extensive security sweep. Ministry of Defense Police officers conducting routine patrols first raised the alarm around 10 p.m. Wednesday after finding an abandoned vehicle near the perimeter. Bomb disposal specialists cleared the vehicle before armed officers discovered a fence breach and located the men inside. Initially detained on suspicion of trespass and criminal damage, both men were arrested again under the National Security Act for allegedly entering a prohibited place for a purpose prejudicial to the United Kingdom. They remain in custody

items.title_original: Woman, 87, dies after being carried from home of 70 years on stretcher during eviction in Spain
items.summary: مرگ یک زن 87 ساله که از خانه دیرینه اش بیرون رانده شده بود، بحران سیاسی در اسپانیا را تشدید کرده است، جایی که اعتراضات سراسری به دلیل افزایش هزینه های مسکن به برگزاری انتخابات زودهنگام کمک کرده است. به گزارش آسوشیتدپرس، ماریا دل کارمن آباسکال، معروف به "ماریکارمن" روز چهارشنبه پس از اخراج از آپارتمانی در مادرید که هفت دهه در آن زندگی می کرد، در بیمارستان بستری شد. مرگ او تنها چند روز پس از آن اتفاق افتاد که پدرو سانچز، نخست وزیر اسپانیا، پس از ناکامی دولتش در تصویب تدابیر اضطراری مسکن در پارلمان، انتخابات زودهنگام را برای 29 نوامبر فراخوان داد. این جنجال فشار جدیدی را بر حزب سوسیالیست سانچز وارد کرده است زیرا اسپانیا با ناامیدی گسترده از افزایش اجاره بها و قیمت مسکن دست و پنجه نرم می کند. تماس رهبر اپوزیسیون اسپانیا
items.summary_original: The death of an 87-year-old woman who was evicted from her longtime home has intensified a political crisis in Spain , where nationwide protests over soaring housing costs have helped force an early election. María del Carmen Abascal, known as "Maricarmen," died Wednesday after being hospitalized following her eviction from a Madrid apartment where she had lived for seven decades, according to The Associated Press. Her death came just days after Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez called a snap election for Nov. 29 after his government's failure to pass emergency housing measures through Parliament. The controversy has put renewed pressure on Sánchez's Socialist Party as Spain grapples with widespread frustration over rising rents and housing affordability . SPANISH OPPOSITION LEADER CALLS PRIME MINISTER A ‘TRAITOR’ OVER CEUTA MIGRANT CRISIS At the center of the uproar was Abascal's Sept. 23 eviction, which drew national attention after images showed the elderly woman, who used a wheelchair, being carried from her apartment on a stretcher. Police had cordoned off the street and removed demonstrators who attempted to stop the eviction. The images sparked demonstrations in Madrid and other Spanish cities, turning Abascal into a symbol of the country's housing crisis. The real estate company responsible for her eviction had sought to lease the apartment at a substantially higher price, according to the AP. items.summary_original: An Iranian anti-regime protester was hanged at dawn Oct. 5 inside Isfahan Central Prison, just hours after marrying his imprisoned fiancée over a jail phone line, The Times reported Thursday. Alireza Sepahi, 25, was executed alongside co-defendant Alireza Raisi after being sentenced to death in the anti-government demonstrations at Isfahan’s Alikhani Square Jan. 8., according to Human Rights Iran . Sepahi and his bride, student activist Mahshad Keshani, 22, knew and loved each other before being arrested during anti-regime demonstrations, the report said. IRAN HANGS 2 PROTESTERS IN PUBLIC, CROWD CRIES 'DISHONORABLE' AS SECURITY FIRES TEAR GAS Keshani, who is serving a five-year sentence, pushed for an informal wedding Sunday as fears mounted that Sepahi’s execution was imminent after a final family summons. The couple exchanged vows over the phone from inside Isfahan prison, joined by their fathers. Human rights lawyer Amirsalar Davoudi facilitated the ceremony by reading the vows for the fathers to bless. Keshani’s family gave a copy of the Quran, a saffron rock candy and a single red rose as a traditional dowry. "It was Mahshad’s idea," Davoudi told The Times. "Even now, I wonder how one young woman can possess such courage." items.title: بی‌طرفی، راستی‌آزمایی و پاسخ‌گویی؛ چرا بی‌بی‌سی فارسی بر این اصول ایستادگی می‌کند؟
items.summary: این مطلب توضیح می‌دهد که چرا بی‌بی‌سی فارسی در یکی از پرتنش‌ترین دوره‌های تاریخ معاصر ایران بر اصول بنیادین روزنامه‌نگاری، از جمله بی‌طرفی، راستی‌آزمایی، استقلال تحریریه و پاسخ‌گویی، پافشاری می‌کند. در این مقاله، با مرور شیوه تصمیم‌گیری‌های تحریریه، فرآیند راستی‌آزمایی اخبار، نحوه انتخاب مهمانان و برخورد با خطاها و انتقادها، تشریح می‌شود که هدف بی‌بی‌سی نه جانبداری از هیچ طرف، بلکه ارائه گزارشی دقیق، مستقل و مبتنی بر شواهد است تا مخاطبان بتوانند بر اساس اطلاعات قابل اعتماد، خود درباره رویدادها قضاوت کنند.

items.title: 'کودتای خزنده' در سپاه؛ نوار صوتی جلسه‌ای محرمانه در زمان جنگ
items.summary: با گذشت چهل سال از آغاز جنگ ایران و عراق، هنوز اطلاعات مرتبط با مقاطع مهمی از جنگ، از آرشیوهای محرمانه خارج نشده است. یکی از جلسات مهمی که در آن فرماندهی جنگ مورد انتقاد سپاهیان ناراضی قرار می‌گیرد، اوایل آذر ۶۳ برگزار می‌شود که در دهه‌های اخیر، رسانه‌های حکومتی ایران روایت‌های پراکنده و به‌شدت تحریف شده‌ای را از آن منتشر کرده‌اند.
